To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the string in a self-interacting BF model, the two particles in a BF model, and the string coupled to the two particles in another BF model are described by wave functionals whose dependence on the shape of the path (respectively, surface) is eliminated through unitary transformations, and the resulting wave functionals depend only on the shape of an open path (respectively surface) and on the boundary of a path (respectively of a surface).
the topological interaction in quantum mechanics can be described in terms of the shape of the paths (or surfaces) of the particles or strings.

(i) a surface representation can be defined for a self-interacting string in four dimensions, (ii) the topological interaction in $2+3$ dimensions can be described in terms of open paths (and open surfaces), and (iii) the string-particle coupling mediated by a BF field in $3+3$ dimensions is equivalent to the topological coupling of two particles in $2+2$ dimensions, except by the boundary contribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to interacting particles and strings, based on the use of geometric representations.
a generalization of the loop representation to the case of interacting particles and strings.
the study of the geometrical aspects of interacting quantum systems, with the aim to clarify the physical meaning of geometrical representations in quantum field theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the geometrical description of interacting quantum systems can be carried out in a consistent way, provided the coupling constant is suitably quantized.

the topological interaction between strings and particles is naturally represented in the loop representation, and that the geometrical picture of Faraday's surfaces emerges in a natural way in a generalized loop representation.

in the presence of topological interactions the wave functional of the system can be written as a functional of the boundary of the open path or surface, and the boundary dependence can be eliminated through an appropriate unitary transformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in all the cases considered, the geometrical description of the quantum states is consistent, and that it provides a clear picture of the physical phenomena involved.
the topological interactions are naturally described by a path representation, and the non-topological interactions by a surface representation.

, for the models under consideration, the path representation is not a fundamental representation of the theory, but only one of the possible representations that can be obtained from the surface representation by means of a unitary transformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geometric description of the quantum states of interacting particles and strings can be carried over in a natural way from the noninteracting case to that of the interacting one.
the geometric description of interacting systems can be extended beyond the case of the free particle or string.
a geometrical setting for the description of interacting quantum systems can be built, even in the case of nontrivial interactions.
